title: Key Takeaways
intro: The essentials to carry into your next client conversation about private markets.

points.text: Private markets cover private equity, private credit, private real estate, and private infrastructure — companies and assets that never trade on public exchanges.
Deals are negotiated directly between parties, insulating them from daily public-market price swings and offering the potential for stronger risk-adjusted returns and diversification.
Access to that return potential comes with reduced liquidity and multi-year lock-ups, which needs a clear, plain-language conversation before any allocation.
Unlike public index investing, the gap between skilled and unskilled private markets managers is wide, so due diligence on track record and sourcing is critical.
Newer fund structures are opening private markets to individual investors — advisors who build fluency now will be ready as client demand grows.
